lines.say: I do a lot of family work. Family work is often avoided in psychiatry, but I think it can be really helpful. I appreciate you being willing to come in.
Usually, I like to get to know you a little bit. You can share whatever you’d like.
Is there anything anyone wants to make sure we address?
What has made it hard for the two of you to talk about it?
What are you feeling as you hear all of this?
How do you feel hearing it directly from her?
You still make your own decisions.
It really shouldn’t fall on her lap.
The two biggest things are time and consistency.
Trust is lost, and it’s hard to trust yourself to decide who you can trust.
When you feel like you can’t express the anger to that person, someone else is going to get that anger.
Repairing the relationship will make that relationship even stronger.
What is one activity the family could do together that is not focused on a crisis or solving a problem?
Before we stop, is there anything else either of you needs to say?
You can continue spending time together after the meeting if you would like.
